correction_1.truth: it is the GENERATION GUARD's expected-value materialization; direct exits are patched, so the movz/movk stub holding that chain is dead code
correction_1.evidence: independent re-derivation from census raw + snapshots: 15.69% guard-expected vs 0.01% exit_target

correction_2.claim_struck: the guard's ldar cost is acquire ordering (or a D-cache miss on the generation cell)
correction_2.truth: REFUTED by experiment. Generation cells are L1-resident (166 lines = 10.6 KB vs 64 KB L1D). A store-count ladder holding the guard fixed shows ldar, ldapr and plain ldr all cost the same as NO LOAD AT ALL; cost tracks context-STORE count only
correction_2.consequence: the block prologue is STORE-THROUGHPUT-BOUND. The guard's load is where retirement stalls waiting on the store queue, so the drain skids onto it; the five entry stores are the cause

chaining_verdict: UNSOUND and worse than previously recorded: link severing does not exist anywhere in the tree (PublishedBlock retains no links, so there is no reverse index), and trusted entry would degrade the guard from per-block to per-gateway-entry, leaving a self-linked hot loop generation-checked once for its whole lifetime
chaining_salvage: superblock formation IS sound and needs no new safety story: one AssembledBlock means internal edges are dynasm labels, not patched slots, so there is nothing to sever and one guard covers the unit. HARD CONSTRAINT: must not cross a guest page boundary, because the guard is single-page and `sensitive` metadata is keyed (guest_pc, block_generation)
implication: optimize the block prologue by removing STORES, not by tuning the guard's load or its comparison
